title: Procedure
description: AIP schema for procedure-style Instructions: any structured procedure, workflow, or execution graph — runbooks, recipes, pipelines, multi-step playbooks. A procedure is a graph of script-backed nodes (steps) connected by inputs and outputs; conditional logic lives in `scripts/`, not in typed schema fields. Captures trigger conditions, applicability contexts, steps (linear, parallel, branching, or DAG-shaped), execution modes, integrations, and worked scenarios. Scope is the category of work (any procedure), not a specific skill.

name.description: Identifier for this input or output. Downstream steps reference an upstream output by this name via their `inputs`.

type.description: Short type label from the AIP vocabulary: `string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `object`, or `list[*]` (collection of any of the above). See `SKILL.md` § Use Simple Type Vocabulary. Not machine-enforced; detailed checks belong in the backing script.

nullable.description: Optional. When true, the value may be absent. Defaults to false.

description.description: One-line summary of what this input/output represents. Optional but recommended — makes the graph readable without opening the backing script.

purpose.description: What the procedure encapsulates as a coherent unit of work — the scope it covers and what it adds beyond general agent knowledge. One short paragraph.

trigger_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should consider this skill. Mixed granularity expected — immediate invocation triggers (e.g., 'user asks to add functionality') alongside broader applicability contexts (e.g., 'evaluating technology choices') belong in the same list.

do_not_use_when.description: Optional. Conditions under which the agent should NOT use this skill — explicit non-purposes that pair with trigger_when to sharpen activation. Helps the agent calibrate when adjacent skills or general reasoning would serve better.

scope_and_approval.description: Optional. Read-only vs write actions, approval checkpoints, irreversible-action gates, and other constraints on what the procedure may do without human confirmation. Freeform prose.

steps.description: Steps the agent executes — the nodes of the procedure's execution graph. Default ordering is by list position; use `depends_on` for explicit graph dependencies, `parallel` for fan-out within a step, `one_of` for mutually-exclusive alternatives, and `script` to back the node with code (preferred whenever the node's logic can be expressed programmatically).

name.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within this procedure. Other steps reference it via `depends_on`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.

description.description: What the step does. When the node is script-backed, keep this to a one-line summary — the script is the source of truth for the logic.

depends_on.description: Optional. Names of steps that must complete before this one runs. Omit for steps that run in list order. Use to express DAG-shaped procedures.

parallel.description: Optional. True if sub-tasks within this step fan out and run in parallel.

one_of.description: Optional. Mutually exclusive sub-step alternatives; the agent picks exactly one.

script.description: Optional. Relative path under `scripts/` to the script that executes this node. When present, the script is the source of truth for the node's logic; the description is a one-line summary, not instructions. Conditional logic (decisions, branching) belongs here, not in typed schema fields.

inputs.description: Optional. Inputs this node consumes — references to outputs of upstream nodes or to externally supplied values. Forms the incoming edges of the execution graph. Each item declares a `name`, optional `type` (Python annotation — see `SKILL.md` § Type Annotations), and optional one-line `description`.

outputs.description: Optional. Outputs this node produces. Downstream nodes reference these by `name` via their `inputs`. Forms the outgoing edges of the execution graph. Each item declares a `name`, optional `type`, and optional one-line `description`.

modes.description: Optional. Execution modes (e.g., quick inline vs full subagent, dry-run vs apply). Each item is a named mode with a freeform body. Prefer expressing mode-specific *logic* in scripts (gated on a mode flag); use this field for the human-readable description of each variant.

name.description: Short identifier for the mode (e.g., quick, full, dry-run).

search_shortcuts.description: Optional. Reference list of common tools, libraries, services, or lookup targets grouped by category. Each item is a category with a freeform body.

category.description: Category name (e.g., Development Tooling, Data Sources).

body.description: Items in the category as freeform prose.

integrations.description: Optional. How this procedure composes with other agents, skills, or workflows. Each item is a partner with a freeform body so sub-structure (sub-bullets, cycles, etc.) is preserved.

partner.description: Name of the partner agent, skill, or workflow.

body.description: How the integration works, as freeform prose.

scenarios.description: Optional. Worked illustrative examples showing the procedure applied to concrete cases. Documentation, not a runtime decision table — the agent does not iterate `scenarios` to pick an action. Renamed from `examples` to avoid the JSON Schema reserved keyword.

need.description: The functional need or input situation the procedure is applied to.

context.description: Optional. Preceding investigation, lookup, or context-gathering and what it surfaced.

action.description: The action taken or step path chosen.

outcome.description: Optional. The result delivered or value pitch.

anti_patterns.description: Optional. Common mistakes the procedure steers the agent away from. Concrete corrections to errors the agent would otherwise make.
